merger_description:
Infoblox Inc. (**Infoblox**), a company jointly owned by Warburg Pincus LLC (**Warburg Pincus**) and by funds managed and/or controlled by Vista Equity Partners Management, LLC (**Vista**), proposes to acquire 100% of the equity interests in Kentik Technologies, Inc. (**Kentik**).

Warburg Pincus is a global private equity firm headquartered in New York City with more than USD 100 billion in assets under management.

Vista is a US-based private equity firm that focuses on financing enterprise software, data and technology-enabled businesses.

Infoblox is a global provider of IT automation and security services. Infoblox offers core network management and security solutions for Domain Name System (**DNS**), Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (**DHCP**), and Internet Protocol (**IP**) address management across on-premise, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments. It also offers asset discovery, DNS-layer threat protection, security analytics, threat intelligence, and related support, professional, education, and managed services delivered directly and through partners. It is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.

Kentik is a US-based network observability and intelligence software supplier, offering a cloud-based platform that collects, analyses, and contextualises network telemetry data across on-premise, hybrid, and cloud environments. Its network monitoring tools help network administrators to keep track of the health and performance of modern, complex networks. It is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Infoblox and Kentik in
the supply of observability solutions and network
performance monitoring
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of core network management and
security solutions, and observability and network
performance monitoring solutions, post-acquisition
c. LogicMonitor and Kentik’s combined share in the supply of
observability and network performance monitoring solutions
in the Asia-Pacific region, and globally, is low and the
increase in share of supply arising from the Acquisition
would be small
d. there are alternative global suppliers of both core network
management and security solutions, and observability and
network performance monitoring solutions, in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
